issues.legal_issue: An owner remains liable to assessment of agricultural income tax on income derived from the owner’s land when a court-appointed receiver manages the land and collects the income.
material_facts: A court-appointed receiver managed the owner’s estate during the relevant income year and collected income derived from it.
The income was treated as the owner’s agricultural income, and its agricultural character was not disputed before the Court.
The owner was assessed for agricultural income tax on that income.
issues.conclusion: The owner could be assessed and remained liable for tax on the income, even though the receiver managed the estate and collected the income. The provision allowing assessment of the receiver did not exempt the owner; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3 and 2(m) of the Bihar Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1948, agricultural income is charged to tax as the income of every person, and the definition of person includes a receiver. Section 13 permits the receiver to be treated as an assessee and provides a means of recovering tax; it is not a charging provision and does not discharge the owner from liability. The taxing authorities may assess the owner, the receiver, or both as permitted by the Act. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: agricultural_income_tax_assessment and owner_land_income and receiver_managed_and_collected and tax_framework_includes_receivers

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns assessment of tax on agricultural income.
predicates.owner_land_income: Income was derived from land belonging to the owner and was treated as the owner’s income.
predicates.receiver_managed_and_collected: A receiver managed the owner’s land and collected the income derived from it.
predicates.tax_framework_includes_receivers: The governing tax framework allowed a receiver holding property for another to be treated as an assessee.

issues.definition: When an agricultural-income-tax assessment concerns income derived from an owner’s land, a receiver managed the land and collected the income, and the tax framework includes receivers among persons who may be treated as assessees, the owner remains assessable.
